purpose: Persist literal paragraph-level teaching episodes so fresh writers can retrieve the transformation itself rather than only abstract humanization rules.
owner_correction: Whole-article manual rewrites can confound realization changes with new or removed authorial thought. Paragraph-level rewrites that deliberately preserve the AI paragraph's thought are higher-value training evidence. When a model subsequently transfers the correction successfully, preserve that transfer as part of the same episode.

alignment_classes.ALIGNED_SAME_THOUGHT: Before and owner-after carry the same substantive thought/function within ordinary preservation tolerance. Eligible as a realization-learning demonstration.
alignment_classes.OWNER_REAUTHORING: Owner changed, added, removed, or rerouted substantive thought. Valuable authorial cognition, but not a clean style/realization training pair.
alignment_classes.CONTROLLED_REVERSE_ALIGNED_PAIR: Owner-Human text predates a controlled AI-shaped transformation that preserved the same protected claims. May be read in reverse as an aligned AI-to-Human demonstration, but chronology must remain explicit.
alignment_classes.TRANSFER_SUCCESS_WITH_OWNER_INTERVENTION: A model-generated candidate successfully transferred prior owner teaching. Preserve it as transfer evidence; do not relabel the model output as owner prose.
alignment_classes.LEGACY_INDEX_ONLY: Outcome is durably known but exact before/after texts have not yet been recovered into this corpus. Not eligible for literal few-shot retrieval until imported.
alignment_classes.OWNER_ENDORSED_MODEL_REVISION: Literal model-before and model-after judged by Joel to be a golden same-purpose style contrast. Preserve model authorship; endorsement is not a new transfer test or blanket factual approval.

retrieval_policy.selection_basis: semantic/rhetorical operation and failure topology, not phrase similarity
retrieval_policy.anti_imitation_rule: Examples teach transformations, not phrases. Never transplant anecdotes, personal facts, jokes, unusual wording, or content-specific details into a new target.

episodes.topic: Somatic / gradual trauma work and inner-child state
episodes.ai_shaped_before: Physical trauma reactions can persist after the danger has passed, even when you know you're safe. With complex or developmental trauma, direct work on the deepest memory can be overwhelming, so a gradual approach may be enough: Buddhist nun Pema Chodron calls it a “feather touch,” and Peter Levine, the founder of Somatic Experiencing, calls gentle work around the edges “pendulation.” The same limit appears in inner-child therapy: you can know what the younger part needs yet enter the child-state so fully that too little adult perspective remains to provide it.
episodes.owner_human_after:
Physical trauma reactions can continue after the danger is over, even when you know you're safe.

With complex or developmental trauma, going straight for the deepest memory can be overwhelming. Instead of diving off the deep end heroically, take it easy, one step at a time. As Buddhist nun Pema Chodron says, "feather touch" is all it takes to gently open up.  Peter Levine, the founder of Somatic Experiencing, calls this gentle work around the edges, "pendulation."

In inner-child therapy, you can know exactly what the younger part needs and still get pulled so far into the child-state that there isn't enough adult perspective left to give it.

episodes.topic: Forgiveness alongside harm, accountability and boundaries
episodes.model_before: The harm happened, and the boundary still matters. The person is still accountable, and forgiveness may come later on its own.
episodes.owner_endorsed_model_after: They really did hurt us and they still have to answer for it, and our boundary with them still matters, but one day we may find that we have forgiven them.
episodes.full_tested_before: We can not ‘force’ forgiveness on ourselves, it has to come from a place of understanding otherwise it can be bypassing. We just remember that it can all be true at once. The harm happened, and the boundary still matters. The person is still accountable, and forgiveness may come later on its own.
